# `Q-12-25` — Listing Id Collides With Section Id

> A listing's `id` is also the id of a section on the page, so both
> elements claim the same HTML anchor.

## What this means

A heading with no explicit id gets one derived from its text, so
`## Learn more` becomes `<section id="learn-more">`. If a listing on
the same page is also called `learn-more`, the rendered page ends up
with two elements carrying that id:

``` markdown
---
listing:
  - id: learn-more
    contents: posts/*.qmd
---

## Learn more

::: {#learn-more}
:::
```

The section's content is safe — Quarto renders the listing into the
`:::` slot inside the section, not into the section itself — but
`#learn-more` no longer identifies one element. A link to it, a table
of contents entry, and any CSS or JavaScript selecting on the id may
each resolve to whichever element the browser reaches first.

## How to fix

Rename whichever of the two is easier to move.

To rename the listing, change both the `id:` and the slot that
matches it:

``` markdown
---
listing:
  - id: recent-posts
    contents: posts/*.qmd
---

## Learn more

::: {#recent-posts}
:::
```

Or give the heading an explicit id of its own, leaving the listing
alone:

``` markdown
## Learn more {#sec-learn-more}

::: {#learn-more}
:::
```

Note that changing a heading's id changes the anchor readers use to
link to that section, so prefer renaming the listing on a page that is
already published.
